summary.headline: The History of the Transistor: The Foundation of Modern Computation
summary.executive_summary: An authoritative analysis of The History of the Transistor, charting its origins, solid-state mechanisms, and vast computing revolution.
key_takeaways: Discovered through groundbreaking research at Bell Labs.
Replaced fragile vacuum tubes with solid-state semiconductors.
Enabled exponential scaling described by Moore's Law.

claims.claim_text: The invention of the point-contact transistor in December 1947 marked the start of the solid-state electronics era.
claims.visual_cue_suggestion: Historical Bell Labs laboratory setup and original germanium crystal apparatus

claims.claim_text: Transistors control electrical current by altering semiconductor conductivity through applied voltage.
claims.visual_cue_suggestion: 3D atomic schematic showing electron-hole conduction across p-n junction

claims.claim_text: Modern microprocessors integrate over 100 billion transistors on a single silicon die.
